citations.title: Scope
citations.requirement: Ch. 2800 sets minimum licensure requirements for assisted living residences and does not apply to personal care homes, domiciliary care homes, independent living communities or commercial boarding homes. (Text is from a DHS-hosted Pa. Code print; confirm no later amendments.)

citations.title: Inspections and licenses
citations.requirement: DHS makes at least one unannounced onsite inspection a year. The residence must post the current license, the current inspection summary and a copy of Ch. 2800 in a conspicuous public place.

citations.title: Access
citations.requirement: Give immediate access to the residence, residents and records on request to DHS agents, the area agency on aging, the LTC Ombudsman, the P&A system and, if the resident asks, the designated person. Community and legal-services groups get access during visiting hours.

citations.title: Procedural requirements for licensure; special care designation; dual licensure
citations.requirement: DHS inspects before initial licensure and reinspects within 3 months. Fees are $300 plus $75 per bed (per-bed fee CPI-adjustable). Special care designation costs $150. Only licensees may use the term 'assisted living'.

citations.title: Maximum capacity
citations.requirement: Licensed capacity may not be exceeded. A request to increase capacity must be approved by DHS and other authorities before additional residents are admitted.

citations.title: Fire safety approval
citations.requirement: Written fire safety approval is required before licensure. If it is withdrawn or restricted, notify DHS orally at once and in writing within 48 hours. After renovation, submit new approval within 15 days. Renew at least every 3 years.

citations.title: Abuse reporting covered by law
citations.requirement: Immediately report suspected abuse under the Older Adult Protective Services Act and 6 Pa. Code §§15.21–15.27. For staff allegations, supervise or suspend the person at once, notify DHS immediately, and notify the resident and designated person.

citations.title: Reportable incidents and conditions – list and policies
citations.requirement: Defines 20 reportable incidents or conditions, including death, hospital-level injury, rights violations, unexplained absence, fund misuse, outbreaks, fire, med errors and utility termination. Written prevention, reporting and investigation policies are required.

citations.title: Reportable incidents – timelines and reports
citations.requirement: Report to the DHS ALR office or hotline within 24 hours, and tell family and the designated person immediately. Submit a final report on the DHS form after the investigation. Inform affected residents if validated. Keep a copy.

citations.title: Confidentiality of records
citations.requirement: Resident records are confidential. Without written consent, only the resident, designated person, staff providing services, DHS agents and the ombudsman may see them, except in emergencies or on court order.

citations.title: Applicable laws
citations.requirement: The residence must comply with applicable Federal, State and local laws, ordinances and regulations. Violations of health and safety laws are themselves reportable under §2800.16(a)(19).

citations.title: Waivers
citations.requirement: Waivers use the DHS form and require no jeopardy to residents. They get a 30-day public comment period, and residents must be given the request 30 days before it is submitted. Rights, contract, reporting, fire safety, assessment and training rules cannot be waived.

citations.title: Financial management
citations.requirement: If handling resident funds: keep transaction records, disburse within 24 hours, get written receipts, never commingle, and offer an interest-bearing account if over $200 is held more than 2 months. Staff may not hold POA or guardianship. Give itemized quarterly accounts.

citations.title: Application and admission – documents and certification
citations.requirement: Medical evaluation within 60 days before admission and initial assessment within 30 days before. Final support plan within 30 days after admission and contract by 24 hours after. Certify before admission that needs can be met. If not, give a written denial and refer.

citations.title: Written disclosures before admission
citations.requirement: On application, give the non-waivable rights list, the contract, rules and the DHS-approved handbook. Also give service and core-package costs, DHS contact info, inspection-report access, ADA-compliant unit count and any waivers in effect.

citations.title: Resident-residence contract
citations.requirement: The contract runs month-to-month, with 14 days' resident notice and 30 days' residence notice. It must include a fee schedule, refund terms and bed-hold charges. Residents have a 72-hour rescission right, and no life-care asset assignment is allowed.

citations.title: Quality management
citations.requirement: Establish and implement a quality management plan. It must periodically review incident reporting, complaints, staff training, violations and plans of correction, and councils, and it must carry out improvement measures.

citations.title: SSI recipients
citations.requirement: If an SSI-eligible resident is admitted, charges may not exceed monthly income minus the personal needs allowance. Provide hygiene items, laundry and ADL/IADL help at no extra charge. Third-party payments may not be used for food, clothing or shelter.

citations.title: Refunds
citations.requirement: Refund prepaid charges within 30 days of discharge, the personal needs allowance within 2 business days, and managed funds within 2 business days of the unit being cleared. Give an itemized account within 30 days. Death refunds follow the Elder Care Payment Restitution Act for age 60+.

citations.title: Hospice care and services
citations.requirement: Hospice care and services licensed by the Department of Health may be provided in an assisted living residence.

citations.title: Informed consent process
citations.requirement: Either party may start the process when a competent resident's choices create risk. Give oral and written notice with the ombudsman's contact. Put any agreement in writing, update it on condition change, and allow rescission within 30 days. It may not be a condition of admission.

citations.title: Notification of rights and complaint procedures
citations.requirement: At admission, inform residents and designated persons of rights and the right to complain without retaliation. Use a language or mode they understand and post the DHS rights poster. Give a copy and keep a signed acknowledgment.

citations.title: Specific rights
citations.requirement: Rights include non-discrimination, freedom from abuse and restraints, 30 days' written notice of new rules, private phone and mail, ombudsman access, visitors at any time, privacy, records access, physician choice, and relocation assistance.

citations.title: Prohibition against deprivation of rights
citations.requirement: A resident may not be deprived of rights. Rights may not be used as a reward or sanction, and any waiver of a right is void.

citations.title: Complaint procedures
citations.requirement: Before admission, inform residents of the right to complain to DHS, the ombudsman or protective services unit, the Disability Rights Network or police. Keep a complaint log, give a status report within 2 business days and a written decision within 7 days. Post hotline and agency numbers in large print.

citations.title: Criminal history checks; staff hiring, retention and utilization
citations.requirement: Criminal history checks, hiring policies and staff retention must comply with the Older Adult Protective Services Act, 6 Pa. Code Ch. 15, and the Department of Aging's OAPSA hiring policy.

citations.title: Qualifications and responsibilities of administrators
citations.requirement: Administrator must be age 21+ and qualify by RN license plus 1 year of experience in the past 10 years, or by one of the other listed paths. Responsible for operations and compliance. Must know Ch. 2800 and be free of impairing conditions.

citations.title: Qualifications for direct care staff persons
citations.requirement: Direct care staff must be 18+, hold a diploma, GED or active PA nurse aide registry status, and be free of impairing conditions. Volunteers giving ADL help meet the same standards. Food service or housekeeping staff may be 16–17.

citations.title: Administrator staffing
citations.requirement: Administrator present an average of 36+ hours a week each calendar month, at least 30 during business hours. Name a written designee (3,000 operational hours plus competency test) and a written staff person for absences. The administrator or designee must be on call.

citations.title: Direct care staffing; awake staff
citations.requirement: A direct care staff person age 21+ must be in the residence whenever residents are present. Provide at least 1 hour per day of services per mobile resident and 2 hours per day per resident with mobility needs, with 75% in waking hours. Direct care staff must be awake at all times.

citations.title: Additional staffing based on needs of residents
citations.requirement: Staffing must meet assessed needs and the stated levels are only a minimum. Extra hours are required for transportation, laundry, food service, housekeeping and maintenance. A licensed nurse must be available or on call at all times, and a dietician on staff or contract.

citations.title: Substitute personnel; list of staff persons
citations.requirement: Arrange substitutes who meet direct care qualifications and training when scheduled staff are absent. Keep a current list of names, addresses and phone numbers for all staff, substitutes and volunteers.

citations.title: First aid, CPR and obstructed airway training
citations.requirement: For every 35 residents, at least one staff person trained in first aid and certified in obstructed airway and CPR must be present at all times. Training must come from a certified trainer. Staff must provide CPR unless the resident has a DNR.

citations.title: Administrator training and orientation
citations.requirement: Before employment: DHS orientation, a 100-hour DHS-approved course and a passing competency test. Then at least 24 hours of annual training from DHS-approved sources, with written verification to the ALR Licensing Office. Keep training records.

citations.title: Staff orientation and direct care staff person training
citations.requirement: Fire and emergency orientation on the first work day. Rights, abuse reporting, incident reporting and safe management within 40 working hours. No unsupervised care until 18 hours of training and the competency test. 16 hours annually, plus annual fire, rights, OAPSA and falls topics.

citations.title: Staff training plan
citations.requirement: Develop an annual training plan listing each direct care staff person's name, position, duties, required courses and scheduled dates, times and locations. Keep documentation of compliance.

citations.title: Additional dementia-specific training
citations.requirement: Administrative, direct care, ancillary and substitute staff and volunteers need 4 hours of dementia-specific training within 30 days of hire and 2 hours annually, in addition to other required training.

citations.title: Sanitation
citations.requirement: Maintain sanitary conditions with no insect or rodent infestation. Remove trash at least weekly and keep it in covered receptacles. Homes serving 9+ residents on private sewer need written sewage-system approval.

citations.title: Resident living units
citations.requirement: Single units need 225 sq ft in new construction after 1/18/2011 and 160 sq ft in existing facilities. Maximum is 2 residents per unit, and sharing is voluntary and in writing. Each unit needs a lockable door with a master key, a phone jack, thermostats and an emergency notification system.

citations.title: Food service; dining room; laundry
citations.requirement: Safe food storage: refrigerated at or below 40°F, frozen at or below 0°F, with thermometers. Common dining space at 15 sq ft per person. Linens changed at least weekly and clothing returned within 24 hours. Laundry is free for SSI residents.

citations.title: Emergency preparedness
citations.requirement: Administrator must have the municipal emergency plan. Written procedures cover designated contacts, medical information, agency numbers, relocation transport, staff duties and utility outages. Keep a 3-day food and water supply. Review and submit the procedures annually to the local EMA.

citations.title: Firearms and weapons; pets
citations.requirement: Have a written weapons policy (locked cabinet, separate ammunition, key held by the administrator or designee). Rules must say whether pets are allowed. Cats and dogs need current rabies certificates, and pet charges go in the contract.

citations.title: Egress, exits, evacuation and fire official notice
citations.requirement: Egress routes stay unlocked and unobstructed. Two independent exits per floor. Post emergency procedures, and post floor diagrams if 9+ residents. A fire-safe area is required for mobility-need residents above or below grade. Notify the local fire department in writing.

citations.title: Smoke detectors, fire alarms and fire extinguishers
citations.requirement: Smoke detector in each living unit, tested monthly with a written record. Repair within 48 hours. Interconnected alarm if 9+ residents, and a monitored connection if 5+ have mobility needs. 2-A extinguishers per floor and every 3,000 sq ft, plus 2A-10BC in the kitchen. Annual inspection.

citations.title: Fire drills
citations.requirement: Unannounced drill monthly, one during sleeping hours every 6 months, and an annual fire safety expert inspection and drill. Vary days, times and exits. Written record per drill. Residents must evacuate within the time set in writing by a fire safety expert.

citations.title: Resident medical evaluation and health care
citations.requirement: Medical evaluation on the DHS form by a physician, PA or CRNP covering diagnosis, allergies, medications, mobility and a TB test within 2 years (or within 15 days of admission). Repeat at least annually and when the medical condition changes.

citations.title: Assistance with medical care; emergency medical plan
citations.requirement: Help residents secure medical care. Document refusals and efforts to obtain consent. Keep a written emergency medical plan (hospital, transport, staffing). Emergency data, including advance directives and DNR, must go with the resident.

citations.title: Use of tobacco
citations.requirement: Residence rules must say whether it is smoking or nonsmoking. If smoking is permitted, adopt written fire-safety policies: designated area, fireproof receptacles, extinguishers, no tobacco use during transportation, and no smoking outside the designated area.

citations.title: Nutrition; meals; withholding or forcing food
citations.requirement: Three meals daily meeting USDA allowances, with an alternative item, plus snacks. Maximum gaps are 15 hours overnight and 6 hours between meals. One-week menus posted. Meet prescribed diets. Notify the physician and designated person if a resident refuses food or drink for 24 hours.

citations.title: Transportation
citations.requirement: Provide or arrange transport weekly. Drivers must be 18+ and licensed. Vehicles need a first aid kit and records (registration, insurance, inspection), and one wheelchair-accessible vehicle if supplied. Pick up within 15 minutes of the scheduled time.

citations.title: Self-administration; medication administration
citations.requirement: Assist with self-administration per assessment, and a physician, PA or CRNP must assess residents who self-administer. Staff may administer only if licensed or if they completed DHS-approved training (oral, topical, eye/nose/ear, insulin, epinephrine).

citations.title: Medication storage, disposal, labeling and accountability
citations.requirement: Keep medications and syringes locked in labeled original containers, and do not remove them more than 2 hours before administration. Destroy discontinued or expired medications safely, and send a departing resident's medications along. Keep receipt documentation and a missing-medication process.

citations.title: Prescriptions, medication records, errors and adverse reactions
citations.requirement: Written prescriber orders and a medication record per administration. Report refusals to the prescriber within 24 hours. Report errors immediately to the resident, designated person and prescriber. Document errors and follow-up. Consult a physician at once for adverse reactions.

citations.title: Medication administration training; resident education
citations.requirement: Medication course with performance test passed within the past 2 years. Insulin also requires DHS-approved diabetes education within the past 12 months. Keep training records. Educate and document each resident's right to question or refuse a medication.

citations.title: Safe management techniques; prohibitions; bedside rails
citations.requirement: Use positive interventions. Seclusion, aversive conditioning, pressure points, and chemical, mechanical and manual restraints are prohibited. Bedside rails only if the resident can operate them, with half-length rails only and documented assessment and consent.

citations.title: Service provision; activities; description of services
citations.requirement: Provide the §2800.220(b) service list (meals, laundry, activities, ADL/IADL help, medication help, housekeeping, transport, 24-hour supervision, cognitive support) and Independent and Enhanced core packages. Keep a written description of services with admission and discharge criteria and written procedures.

citations.title: Assessments and support plans
citations.requirement: Initial assessment and preliminary support plan by an RN, LPN under RN, administrator or designee. Reassess annually and on significant change. Final support plan within 30 days of admission, reviewed quarterly, signed, and given to the resident. Notify DHS of mobility needs.

citations.title: Transfer and discharge
citations.requirement: Give 30 days' written notice stating reason, date, destination and ombudsman contact. Closure needs 60 days' notice to DHS. Discharge is allowed only on the listed grounds, with aging-in-place accommodation attempted first. Keep a discharge tracking chart.

citations.title: Excludable conditions; exceptions
citations.requirement: Do not admit or retain residents with ventilator dependency, unhealed Stage III/IV ulcers, continuous IV fluids, communicable-state infectious disease, NG tubes, restraints or 24-hour skilled nursing, unless DHS grants an exception. Keep exception records.

citations.title: Special care units (dementia)
citations.requirement: Apply 60 days before opening a unit. Cognitive screening within 72 hours before admission and quarterly reassessment. 8 hours' initial and 8 hours' annual staff training. Weekly activities, lock approvals, wandering measures, and the 2-hour-per-day staffing rule for every resident.

citations.title: Resident records
citations.requirement: Separate on-site record per resident with the 28 required content items. Retain for 3 years after death or discharge or until audit or litigation ends. Destroy confidentially with a destruction log. Adopt a written record security policy, with records kept locked.

citations.title: Enforcement: violation classes, penalties, revocation, ban on admissions
citations.requirement: Class I violations are $20 per resident per day and must be corrected within 24 hours. Class II is $5–$15 per resident per day. Operating unlicensed is $500 plus $20 per resident per day. Residents must be notified of violations. DHS may ban admissions.

citations.title: Procedural requirements for licensure of personal care homes (PCH)
citations.requirement: PCHs are inspected before licensure and reinspected within 3 months. Application fee by beds: $15 (0–20), $20 (21–50), $30 (51–100), $50 (101+). Ch. 20 applies to PCHs.

citations.title: State plan for regulating and licensing PCHs and ALRs
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for DHS licensing of personal care homes and assisted living residences, including at least one annual unannounced onsite inspection of each.

policies.title: SCU Program Information and General SCU Information
state_specifics: Program information under §2800.237(a)(1)-(6)
General SCU information under §2800.239(a), (c)(1)-(22)
Cognitive screening within 72 hours before admission; quarterly reassessment
Weekly activities program
PCH parallel: secured dementia care unit rules, §2600.231-.239

policies.title: Resident-Residence Contract and Admission Disclosures
state_specifics: Month-to-month; 14 days' resident notice, 30 days' residence notice (§2800.25)
Must include fee schedule, refund terms, bed-hold charges and pet charges
Residents have a 72-hour rescission right; no life-care asset assignment
On application give the rights list, contract, rules, DHS-approved handbook, service and core-package costs, and DHS contact info (§2800.22(e))
Refund prepaid charges within 30 days of discharge

policies.title: Resident Medical Evaluation and Health Care Form
state_specifics: DHS form completed by a physician, PA or CRNP (§2800.141)
Covers diagnosis, allergies, medications, mobility and TB test within 2 years (or within 15 days of admission)
Completed within 60 days before admission; repeat at least annually and on change in medical condition

policies.title: Initial Assessment, Additional Assessments and Support Plan Forms
state_specifics: Initial assessment and preliminary support plan within 30 days before admission (§2800.224)
Reassess annually and on significant change (§2800.225)
Final support plan within 30 days of admission, reviewed quarterly, signed and given to the resident (§2800.227)
Notify DHS of mobility needs
PCH parallel: preadmission screening form (§2600.224), assessment form (§2600.225), support plan form (§2600.227)

policies.title: Forms Library, Fire Drill Record, Rights Poster and Document Control
state_specifics: Written fire drill record for every drill (§2800.132(c))
Rights poster per §2800.41
Medication administration record per §2800.187(a)
Keep a controlled master set with version dates; review annually
Post the license, current inspection summary and a copy of Ch. 2800 (§2800.3)

policies.title: Fire-Retardant Mattress Compliance
state_specifics: DHS prelicensure item: document mattress fire-retardant compliance
Keep manufacturer labels or certificates for each mattress
Confirm the accepted standard with BHSL before purchase

policies.title: Water Source Documentation
state_specifics: Document whether water is public or private
Keep the water-supply documentation DHS requires in the prelicensure package
Bottled-water contract applies if a 3-day water supply is not stored (§2800.107)

policies.title: Sewer Source Documentation
state_specifics: Document public or private sewer
Homes serving 9+ residents on private sewer need written sewage-system approval (§2800.85)

policies.category: 14. Legal entity statement of members and affiliated facilities
policies.title: Legal Entity Statement of Members and Affiliated Facilities
state_specifics: List all members/owners and any affiliated facilities
Licensee name must match the entity exactly
Keep current; update DHS on ownership changes

policies.title: List of Consultants
state_specifics: List the contracted licensed nurse, dietitian and fire safety expert
Include contract scope and license information
Fire safety expert performs the annual inspection and drill

policies.title: Staff List and Organizational Chart
state_specifics: Keep a current list of names, addresses and phone numbers for all staff, substitutes and volunteers (§2800.62)
Show administrator, designee and on-call arrangements on the chart

policies.title: Affidavits and Attestations (if applicable)
state_specifics: Submit only if DHS requires an affidavit for your application
Confirm the current affidavit form and content with BHSL
Retain signed copies in the licensing file

policies.title: Management Agreements (if applicable)
state_specifics: Submit any management agreement with the application
The licensee remains responsible for compliance with Ch. 2800
Disclose the manager's affiliated facilities in the legal entity statement

policies.title: Licensure, Posting, Waivers, Inspections and Regulatory Compliance
state_specifics: At least one unannounced annual inspection; reinspection within 3 months of initial licensure
Post license, inspection summary and Ch. 2800 copy in a conspicuous public place
Waivers use the DHS form with 30-day public comment; residents get the request 30 days before submission
Class I violations are $20 per resident per day, corrected within 24 hours; operating unlicensed is $500 plus $20 per resident per day
Policy review and corporate compliance follow the forms control policy

policies.title: Fees, Deposits, Refunds, Resident Funds and Personal Property
state_specifics: If handling resident funds: keep transaction records, disburse within 24 hours, no commingling, written receipts
Offer an interest-bearing account if over $200 is held more than 2 months; itemized quarterly accounts
Staff may not hold POA or guardianship
Refund personal needs allowance within 2 business days and itemized account within 30 days
Death refunds follow the Elder Care Payment Restitution Act for age 60+

policies.title: Advance Directives and Informed Consent Process
state_specifics: Informed consent process: oral and written notice with the ombudsman's contact (§2800.30)
Written agreement, updated on condition change; resident may rescind within 30 days
It may not be a condition of admission
Advance directives and DNR travel with the resident in emergencies

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: Give rights notices in a language or mode the resident understands (§2800.41)
Non-discrimination is a listed resident right (§2800.42)
Disclose the number of ADA-compliant units at application (§2800.22(e))

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening, Admission Criteria and Certification
state_specifics: Medical evaluation within 60 days before admission; initial assessment within 30 days before
Certify before admission that needs can be met; otherwise give a written denial and refer
Do not admit residents with excludable conditions unless DHS grants an exception
Provide required disclosures and the DHS-approved handbook on application

policies.title: Nursing Services, Change of Condition and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: Licensed nurse available or on call at all times (§2800.60)
Reassess on significant change and update the support plan
Help residents secure medical care; notify physician and designated person
Death, hospital-level injury and unexplained absence are reportable within 24 hours

policies.title: Hospice, Home Health Coordination and Death of a Resident
state_specifics: Hospice licensed by the Department of Health may serve residents in the residence
A resident's death is a reportable incident (§2800.16)
Death refunds follow the Elder Care Payment Restitution Act for age 60+
Return personal property and managed funds within 2 business days of clearing the unit

policies.title: Falls Prevention and Skin Integrity
state_specifics: Annual falls training for direct care staff (§2800.65)
Unhealed Stage III/IV pressure ulcers are an excludable condition absent DHS exception
Bedside rails only if the resident can operate them; half-length only, with documented assessment and consent
Hospital-level injury is reportable

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Report suspected abuse immediately under OAPSA and 6 Pa. Code §§15.21-15.27 (§2800.15)
For staff allegations: supervise or suspend at once and notify DHS immediately
Notify the resident and designated person
Annual OAPSA training for direct care staff

policies.title: Restraints, Safe Management Techniques and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: Use positive interventions (§2800.201)
Seclusion, aversive conditioning, pressure points, and chemical, mechanical and manual restraints are prohibited (§2800.202)
Staff are trained in safe management within 40 working hours of hire

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Unexplained absence is a reportable incident (24 hours)
Egress routes stay unlocked and unobstructed unless lock approvals are in place
SCU wandering measures and lock approvals apply

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Fire Drills
state_specifics: Unannounced drill monthly; one during sleeping hours every 6 months; annual fire safety expert inspection and drill
Vary days, times and exits; written record per drill
Smoke detectors tested monthly; extinguishers inspected annually
Post emergency procedures; floor diagrams if 9+ residents
Notify the local fire department in writing

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: TB test within 2 years (or within 15 days of admission) for each resident
Outbreaks are reportable incidents
Maintain sanitary conditions; no insect or rodent infestation; trash removed at least weekly

policies.title: Food Service and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: Three meals daily meeting USDA allowances, with an alternative item, plus snacks
Maximum gaps: 15 hours overnight and 6 hours between meals
One-week menus posted; meet prescribed diets with a dietitian
Refrigerate at or below 40°F, freeze at or below 0°F, with thermometers
Notify physician and designated person if a resident refuses food or drink for 24 hours

policies.title: Activities, Transportation, Housekeeping and Laundry
state_specifics: Daily activities program is a required service (§2800.220)
Provide or arrange transportation weekly; drivers 18+ and licensed; pickup within 15 minutes of schedule
Vehicle needs a first aid kit and registration, insurance and inspection records
Linens changed at least weekly; clothing returned within 24 hours
Laundry is free for SSI residents

official.notes: Each checklist is submitted to the BHSL headquarters office before the initial inspection of a new facility, or of a sale or change of legal entity, is scheduled. The checklist says BHSL may request additional materials, or the materials in a different order than listed. The reviewer therefore expects the packet to follow the checklist's own numbering (1-18, with lettered sub-items), with each policy labelled by item number and regulation cite (e.g., '8(a) Reportable Incidents and Conditions Policy – § 2800.16(b)'). The ALR (Ch. 2800) and PCH (Ch. 2600) checklists are separate; a facility licensed as an ALR submits the ALR version and a PCH submits the PCH version. 'doc': 0 is the ALR checklist and 'doc': 1 is the PCH checklist. Items I left out of required_items as application or evidence paperwork, not policy content: 1 (administrator credentials), 2 (the criminal history clearances themselves), 7 (floor plans, elevator certificate, SCU/SDCU site evidence), 9(a) (written SCU/SDCU request), and 11-18. Item 1 (administrator qualifications) is also omitted from required_items, and it is the only omitted item that is partly staffing content. Item 10 is a list of 'forms' (contract, rights poster, fire drill record, assessment and support plan forms, MAR). I kept those as operating documents, not application forms. Drop them if you want strictly written policies. Special Care Unit / Secured Dementia Care Unit items and swimming pool, firearms and smoking policies apply only if applicable. The checklist for the Certificate of Compliance application (hs633-checklist.pdf) covers non-policy paperwork such as fees, occupancy permit and civil rights form. I did not use it. Those fees are not stated consistently across sources (for example, per-bed amounts), so check the current fee schedule. The Ch. 2800 and Ch. 2600 regulation sections cited in brackets are the authority for the content of each policy. I could not open the pacodeandbulletin.gov pages, so each policy's required contents come from the regulation text, which I did not read.
